title: What is the digital root of 9a + 36b + 13?
description: A number is written as 9a + 36b + 13, with whole numbers a and b. The first two parts are multiples of nine, so they leave no remainder, and only thirteen decides the digital root. A check with one for each letter confirms it.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiples of nine leave no remainder on division by nine, so only the part that is not a multiple of nine decides the digital root. Watch for students who try to guess values for a and b instead of using the multiples of nine.

video_script.why: A learner uses the link between the digital root and the remainder on division by nine to find the root of an expression with two letters.
video_script.anchor: the expression 9a + 36b + 13 with its three parts marked
maths_rules: 9a is a multiple of 9; 36b = 9 × 4b is a multiple of 9; both leave no remainder on division by 9
the number leaves the same remainder as 13, and 13 = 9 + 4 leaves 4
video_script.design: One idea: multiples of nine leave no remainder, so only thirteen decides the digital root. Assumes the link between the digital root and the remainder on division by nine. The expression stays on the board all video.
